changes: Four new warm-gradient themes — Gold, Silver, Beige, and Amber — added to Settings. The header takes on a subtle gradient sheen to match.
New Books section — read the written works of Hajee Mahboob Kassim (9 books now, more coming). Each book has chapters, quick chapter jumping, list or slide view, reading progress, and easy sharing.
A dedicated Books page with cover cards to browse the library.
Fixed: events happening today no longer appear twice — once in Today's Events and again in Upcoming Events.
Three new themes! Indigo, Teal, and a true-black OLED dark mode that saves battery on OLED screens.
Theme picker now shows colored swatch circles at a glance, instead of text buttons.

A friendly guided tour now welcomes first-time visitors — choose your language, then walk through the home cards, reading, counter and navigation. You can skip it, or replay it any time from Settings; when you finish, you land back on the home page.
Calendar now shows ALL of today's events (split into Monthly and Other) instead of just the next event
Fixed the gap between the counter bar and the bottom navigation bar
Fixed the Hijri calendar grid navigation so all months are reachable
Fixed the event list jumping back to the top while scrolling
Islamic calendar now includes 2,350 Blessed Days events — Urs (passing) dates, birthdays and special nights across all Hijri months
New Rose theme added to Settings
Font size choices extended — X-Small (12px) to XX-Large (24px)
Calendar grid and Hijri strip show capped event dots (+N marker) so busy dates stay compact
Calendar events grouped into Monthly and Other sections, side by side, with scrollable lists
Calendar event lists now responsive on mobile
Tap the Hijri date strip at the top of any page to open the Islamic Calendar
Calendar events can repeat every month on a chosen Hijri date

Today's Hijri + Gregorian date shown in a thin strip below the header on every page
Hijri Calendar: today's Islamic date, upcoming event countdown, and events mapped automatically
Monthly recurring events — repeat on the same Hijri date every month
